content: The use of minocycline may lead to oral thrush or the development of a new yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This document does not provide a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, contact your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before starting minocycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other tetracyclines (such as doxycycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Minocycline may cause dizziness, which can be exacerbated by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Minocycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Children under 8 years old may be more susceptible to side effects, particularly tooth discoloration, which has also been observed in older children and young adults. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. Pregnancy should be avoided while using minocycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Minocycline may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine catecholamine levels, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts and kidney or liver function tests, may be conducted while you are taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking expired minocycline can cause serious illness. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
